skill.description: Guide ERC-8004 agent identity, reputation, validation, and A2A discovery workflows on Starknet using TypeScript examples.
skill.summary: Build and manage ERC-8004 agent identities and trust signals on Starknet.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, reference links, example URLs, and the public well-known discovery path. Real risks remain around raw private-key handling, funded on-chain transactions, unpinned dependencies, and reputation inherited after identity transfer. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The registration example accepts a raw privateKey variable for a funded account.
remediation.suggestion: Use a hardware wallet, browser wallet, or managed signer. Never place private keys in prompts, source files, logs, or environment examples.

remediation.issue: Examples submit state-changing transactions without an explicit user confirmation boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation of network, contract address, calldata, fees, and signer before every write. Test first with disposable testnet accounts.

remediation.issue: The installation command does not pin the starknet package version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed version and commit the package lockfile. Re-test examples before dependency upgrades.

remediation.issue: Reputation follows the identity NFT after ownership changes.
remediation.suggestion: Refresh ownership before trust decisions and display transfer history. Treat reputation as identity history, not proof of the current operator.

semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to use a funded account and submit registry transactions. Execution can spend fees and create irreversible on-chain state changes.

semantic_findings.title: Reputation Persists Across Ownership Transfer
semantic_findings.description: A new NFT owner inherits the existing reputation. Consumers may misattribute prior trust to a different operator after transfer.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The security considerations explicitly state that a new owner inherits reputation when the agent identity NFT transfers.

content.user_title: Build ERC-8004 Agent Identity on Starknet
content.value_statement: On-chain agent identity requires coordinated registry, signature, and metadata handling. This skill provides Starknet examples for registration, reputation, validation, and A2A discovery.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to register ERC-8004 agent identity NFTs with metadata and IPFS token references.
Shows how to query agent existence, ownership, metadata, and registry totals.
Demonstrates signed feedback authorization and reputation queries.
Demonstrates validation requests, responses, summaries, and status queries.
Provides an A2A Agent Card example linked to Starknet identity data.
limitations: Does not provide deployed registry addresses, ABIs, or complete runnable project files.
Requires a funded Starknet account, secure signing setup, and the starknet package.
Examples use placeholders and may need adaptation for the selected ERC-8004 implementation.
Does not audit contracts, verify validators, or guarantee transaction success.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Registries
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the ERC-8004 identity, reputation, and validation registries on Starknet. Describe how they interact and list required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Agent Registration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Starknet TypeScript registration plan for my agent. Identify metadata, registry address, ABI, signer, RPC, fees, and confirmation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Reputation Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a signed feedback flow for agent {agentId}. Include authorization fields, expiry, replay protection, submission, error handling, and reputation queries.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Identity and A2A
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced integration linking ERC-8004 identity, reputation, validation, and an A2A Agent Card. Include ownership changes, retries, and security checks.

output_examples.input: How should agent feedback authorization work?
output_examples.output: A scoped authorization flow covering owner signature, client address, expiry, chain context, submission limits, verification, and reputation queries.

output_examples.input: Plan an A2A profile linked to ERC-8004 identity.
output_examples.output: An integration plan mapping Agent Card fields to registry identity, reputation, validation, ownership refresh, and the public discovery endpoint.

best_practices: Use secure wallet providers and never place private keys in prompts, source files, or logs.
Confirm network, registry addresses, ABI versions, fees, and calldata before signing.
Re-fetch ownership and authorization state before feedback, validation, or metadata updates.
anti_patterns: Do not run examples on mainnet before testing with disposable accounts and verified contracts.
Do not trust scores without checking provenance, recency, ownership changes, and validator policy.
Do not expose private keys, signed authorizations, or bearer tokens in logs or Agent Cards.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy ERC-8004 contracts?
faq.answer: No. It assumes compatible registries already exist and requires their addresses and ABIs.

faq.question: Does it manage private keys securely?
faq.answer: No. The examples use a privateKey placeholder. Use a secure wallet, hardware signer, or managed key service.

faq.question: Can I use it on mainnet?
faq.answer: Yes, after testnet validation and manual confirmation of network, registry addresses, fees, calldata, and signer permissions.

faq.question: What does the reputation flow require?
faq.answer: The agent owner signs a scoped authorization. The client submits feedback with that authorization and signature.

faq.question: Does it include A2A discovery?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an Agent Card example and the standard well-known discovery path.

faq.question: Can reputation survive ownership transfer?
faq.answer: Yes. Reputation follows the identity NFT, so consumers must display current ownership and transfer history.
